title: Add residency-guard CLI and audit-fanout adapter for per-operator KMS attribution
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers running Private deployments asked for a small, auditable control-plane tool to assert and prove per-operator residency decisions and to attribute KMS usage back to operator tokens. This PR introduces a lightweight CLI 'residency-guard' for operator-side residency checks and an audit-fanout adapter that tags and routes KMS usage events into the audit pipeline. The goal is minimal runtime footprint, clear audit trails, and compatibility with existing RBAC v2 enforcement and the private-installer flow.

Changes:
1) residency-guard CLI (Go): validates operator claims, enforces geozone mappings, consults residency policy cache, and emits signed proof blobs for downstream KMS allocation.
2) kms-usage-attributor (adapter): receives proof blobs and attaches operator-scoped attribution metadata to KMS request envelopes; forwards enriched audit events to audit-fanout (supports both Kafka and HTTP sink).
3) RBAC v2 shim updates: add an attribute matcher for operator.region_hint and operator_tier to allow conditional policy paths.
4) Tests and integration harness: unit tests for policy evaluation, e2e harness stubs for Private installer compatibility, CI job additions.
5) Docs: CLI quickstart and operator checklist.

Commits:
- 9a4b2d2: initial residency-guard CLI scaffold and basic policy evaluator
- 7c3f14a: implement signed-proof blob format and verification helpers
- b6d2a11: kms-usage-attributor adapter and audit-fanout integration (Kafka + HTTP)
- 3f1e00c: RBAC v2 attribute matcher and policy examples
- d2a7f9f: tests, docs, CI job and changelog.

Files changed (high level):
- cmd/residency-guard/main.go (CLI entrypoint)
- internal/policy/evaluator.go (policy cache + matcher)
- internal/proofs/signer.go (signed proof format)
- adapters/kms-attributor/adapter.go (enrichment + fanout)
- adapters/kms-attributor/config.yaml.example
- rbac/policy-templates/operator-region-attribute.yaml
- test/integration/residency-harness/README.md
- docs/enterprise/operator-residency-quickstart.md
- ci/ci-residency-guard.yml
- examples/private-installer/residency-hook.tf
- pkg/audit/fanout/kafka.go
- CHANGELOG.md

Review conversation (summary):
- Diego: requested stronger defensive parsing on proof blobs and explicit versioning header for migration safety. Author reply: added header v1 and backwards-compatibility checks; updated signer helpers with strict bounds.
- Priya: flagged potential race in policy cache refresh during failover; asked for a short-term fix plus TODO for cache topology work. Author reply: implemented lock-free refresh with copy-on-write semantics and added integration test that simulates failover timing.
- Liam: asked to keep the CLI binary small and avoid importing heavy Kafka client into core binary. Author reply: split adapter as separate module and provided lightweight HTTP-only mode for operators that prefer it.
- Security review: Snyk scan indicated an indirect dep flagged; bumped the dep and re-ran tests.

CI summary: New CI job (ci-residency-guard) runs unit, lint, and a short e2e harness against a local mock KMS + audit sink. First run: lint error fixed in commit d2a7f9f; second run: all checks green.

Migration notes:
- Add operator-region attribute to RBAC policy bundles via a staged rollout (rbacv2 shadow + reporting enabled for two weeks).
- Private-installer hook path added; operators must install the CLI on control-plane nodes and configure the residency-hook in the installer manifest.
- Backwards compatibility: adapters accept empty proof blobs but will mark events as unauthenticated (policy decision still enforced server-side).

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main and deploy adapter in shadow mode to audit pipeline.
2) Ship CLI as beta on private-installer channel and notify enterprise customers.
3) Enable RBAC attribute matcher in a staged canary (10% traffic) then full rollout.

Release notes: Adds "residency-guard" CLI to assert operator residency and a kms-usage-attributor adapter that enriches audit events with operator-scoped KMS attribution. See docs/enterprise/operator-residency-quickstart.md for setup instructions.

Why this is different: Existing residency and KMS work focused on server-side decisioning and routing. This change introduces a small, auditable operator-side assertor and an explicit attribution path into the audit pipeline to aid forensic tracing and compliance reporting.

testing_instructions: Unit tests: 'go test ./internal/... ./cmd/residency-guard/...'. Integration: follow test/integration/residency-harness/README.md to start mock-kms and mock-audit-sink, then run './cmd/residency-guard/residency-guard --policy ./rbac/policy-templates/operator-region-attribute.yaml --signing-key ./test/keys/operator.pem' to emit proof; then run adapter in HTTP mode to validate fanout. Verify that audit events contain 'operator_id' and 'operator_region' attributes and that the signed_proof header validates.
